intro.title: Stranger Sharing Calculator
intro.body: How much do you reveal to someone you just met — on a flight, in a queue, at a mixer, or in DMs? Pick the scene and who you're talking to. Get a witty, privacy-smart profile. Everything stays in your browser.

setup.title: Set the scene
setup.subtitle: This tunes a few questions and insights — not a grade on your personality.

place.queue: Line, waiting room, or shared ride

counterpart.prying: Curious fast — lots of personal questions

goal.warmButGuarded: Be warm, keep private things private
goal.checkBoundaries: Test whether this person feels safe

profiles.warm-fence: Warm fence — invite in, lock the vault

insights.dim-privacyGuard-high: Your privacy guard is strong: you share themes, not case files. Keep that — warmth doesn't require proof.
insights.dim-privacyGuard-low: Details slip out before you've decided they're earned. Practice the three-layer rule before the next chat.
insights.dim-socialGrace-high: You navigate awkward chats with grace — exits, pivots, and kindness without interrogation.
insights.dim-socialGrace-low: Conversations stall or snap shut. A bridge question beats a hard door slam.
insights.dim-gutInstinct-high: You notice vibe shifts — flattery, pressure, audience — and adjust before regret hits.
insights.dim-gutInstinct-low: You override the inner "nope" to be nice. Politeness isn't consent to every question.
insights.overall-strong: Overall you're sharing like an adult at a party: connected, bounded, recoverable if you slip.
insights.overall-steady: You're in human middle ground — good instincts with a few habits to tighten.
insights.overall-developing: Real social skill, but your filter updates lag behind your friendliness.
insights.overall-needs-care: This pattern asks for a gentle reset: one rule this week, not a personality overhaul.
insights.place-flight: Seatmate chats are captive and cozy — perfect for stories, risky for routines and employers.
insights.place-queue: Waiting-room talk feels fleeting; strangers still remember names, kids' schools, and complaints.
insights.place-networking: Mixers reward warmth — and punish accidental therapy sessions and client gossip.
insights.place-socialOnline: Online pace blurs intimacy. Slow replies are a feature, not rudeness.
insights.counterpart-pleasant: Friendly energy lowers guards — that's the point, not proof they're family.
insights.counterpart-prying: Fast personal questions aren't intimacy — they're data collection with a smile.
insights.counterpart-professional: Professional context adds permanence: what you say may follow you past the appetizer.
insights.goal-survivePolitely: Surviving politely still allows boundaries — you don't owe a memoir for politeness.
insights.goal-warmButGuarded: Warm + guarded is the sweet spot: they feel seen, your life stays yours.
insights.goal-checkBoundaries: Testing boundaries is smart — watch whether they respect a soft no.

tips.tip-three-layer-rule: Three-layer rule: layer 1 = weather/work genre; layer 2 = feelings in general; layer 3 = names, numbers, addresses — only for trusted people.
tips.tip-swap-detail-for-theme: Swap detail for theme: "Rough quarter at work" beats naming your boss, project, and salary.
tips.tip-no-names-numbers: No names, no numbers: skip exact streets, schools, account hints, and "you can find me @…"
tips.tip-bridge-question: Bridge question: "What got you into that?" moves talk forward without you donating facts.
tips.tip-bathroom-exit: Bathroom / refill exit: physical breaks end chats without a trial about your boundaries.
tips.tip-agree-and-steer: Agree and steer: "Totally — speaking of travel, anywhere you'd go again?"
tips.tip-body-check: Body check: tight chest or urge to overshare = pause, breathe, shorten your next sentence.
tips.tip-delay-answer: Delay answer: "Hmm, let me think" buys time — you don't owe instant autobiography.
tips.tip-curiosity-tax: Curiosity tax: if they ask three personal questions without sharing back, go generic.
tips.tip-post-chat-debrief: Post-chat debrief: two minutes — what did I say I'd rather not repeat? Adjust one habit.
tips.tip-online-slow: Online slow: longer gaps between replies train the right pace — urgency is often artificial.
tips.tip-public-volume: Public volume: if strangers could repeat it, lower the detail — ears travel.

work-crisis-share.prompt: When a stranger asks about work, I keep crisis details off the table.

byPlace.flight: When my seatmate asks what I do and how it's going, I don't unload a workplace crisis.
byPlace.queue: When someone in line asks about my job stress, I don't name bosses, layoffs, or HR drama.
byPlace.networking: At a mixer, when someone probes my company troubles, I stay thematic — not case-specific.
byPlace.socialOnline: In DMs about work, I don't paste in Slack drama, screenshots, or identifiable rants.

options.1: I describe the full meltdown — names, emails, who's wrong
options.2: I vent specifics until I notice their face change
options.3: I mix general stress with one detail I later wish I'd kept
options.4: I say it's been rough but keep names and internal politics out
options.5: I offer a one-line theme and redirect — no dossier

family-drama-line.prompt: When family comes up with a stranger, I don't import live drama.

options.1: I tell the whole saga — who said what, who's not speaking
options.2: I share enough that they could gossip accurately later
options.3: I vent one hot story, then feel weird about it
options.4: I mention "family stuff" without cast lists or timelines
options.5: I stay vague or positive — drama stays at home

money-health-details.prompt: When money or health surfaces in small talk, I keep numbers and diagnoses private.

options.1: I share salaries, debt, test results, or meds by name
options.2: I drop numbers or clinic names before I think
options.3: I share sometimes when the mood feels safe
options.4: I speak in general terms — "tight year," "managing a condition"
options.5: I redirect or keep it surface — not their chart to read

location-routines.prompt: I avoid giving strangers a map of my daily life.

byPlace.flight: On a flight, I don't share my neighborhood, gym times, or kid pickup routes.
byPlace.queue: While waiting, I don't describe where I live, when I'm home alone, or my commute pattern.
byPlace.networking: At events, I don't hand out my home cross-streets or "I'm always at X on Tuesdays."
byPlace.socialOnline: Online, I don't post or say routines that pin down where I am when.

options.1: I describe exact address habits — routes, schedules, who's home when
options.2: I mention my area and regular spots without being asked
options.3: I share if they seem nice or we have something in common
options.4: I say a broad region or "suburbs" — no schedule
options.5: I keep location and routines off the table with strangers

kids-school-info.prompt: When kids or school come up, I protect their identifiers.

options.1: I name schools, teachers, teams, and where we hang after class
options.2: I share enough that someone could spot my kid in a crowd
options.3: I brag with details, then wonder if that was too much
options.4: I talk about ages or interests without school names or schedules
options.5: I keep kids generic — or skip specifics entirely

passwords-or-accounts.prompt: I never treat stranger chat like IT support for my accounts.

options.1: I've hinted at passwords, recovery codes, or login tricks
options.2: I describe security questions or "how I remember passwords"
options.3: I joke about bad password habits with real examples
options.4: I say I use a manager — no demos, no screens
options.5: Account talk stays zero-detail — not a teachable moment with strangers

photos-and-screens.prompt: I don't show strangers my phone gallery or sensitive screens.

byPlace.flight: On a flight, I don't turn my screen or photos toward the seatmate.
byPlace.queue: In a waiting room, I keep chats and photos angled away from neighbors.
byPlace.networking: At a event, I don't pass my phone around with client threads visible.
byPlace.socialOnline: I don't send identifying screenshots or photo dumps to new online contacts.

options.1: I scroll photos or messages where anyone can read along
options.2: I show "one cute pic" that includes addresses, kids, or work chats
options.3: I share screens when asked — feels faster than explaining
options.4: I describe content verbally; phone stays private
options.5: Screens and galleries stay closed — strangers don't get the tour

ex-and-intimacy.prompt: When relationships or intimacy come up, I keep stranger chats PG and private.

options.1: I share explicit stories or identifying ex drama
options.2: I name exes and replay intimate scenes for reaction
options.3: I overshare when wine or vibe makes it feel like friendship
options.4: I stay general — "dating's weird lately" — no play-by-play
options.5: I decline or pivot — my love life isn't seatmate content

exit-politics.prompt: When I need to leave a conversation, I exit without a guilt spiral.

byCounterpart.pleasant: When a nice stranger keeps chatting, I leave kindly — not trapped by their warmth.
byCounterpart.prying: When someone digs in with questions, I exit without apologizing for having boundaries.
byCounterpart.professional: When a contact monopolizes me, I leave with a clean professional line.

options.1: I stay too long, then ghost or lie badly later
options.2: I wait until I'm annoyed and leave abruptly
options.3: I hint I should go but keep answering one more question
options.4: I use a clear line — bathroom, call, next session — and go
options.5: I exit early and warm: thanks, enjoyed it, gotta run

deflect-personal-q.prompt: When someone asks something too personal, I deflect without a confession.

byCounterpart.pleasant: When a friendly stranger asks where I live or if I'm single, I answer lightly — not fully.
byCounterpart.prying: When a prying person pushes for salary, relationship, or address, I block without debating.
byCounterpart.professional: When a work contact asks personal questions, I redirect to business-appropriate ground.

options.1: I answer because it feels rude not to — then regret it
options.2: I answer half, then try to walk it back awkwardly
options.3: I joke away sometimes; other times I spill
options.4: I use a soft no or vague answer — "around town," "complicated week"
options.5: I redirect cleanly: "Still figuring that out — how about you?"

match-their-depth.prompt: I match a stranger's depth — I don't under-share or flood to keep pace.

options.1: I dump heavy life stuff because they shared first
options.2: I escalate intimacy faster than the relationship earned
options.3: I mirror them exactly — even when I should stay shallow
options.4: I stay one half-step lighter than their depth
options.5: I choose my layer deliberately — not copy-paste intimacy

change-topic-smooth.prompt: When a topic gets too hot, I pivot without making it weird.

options.1: I freeze or snap "let's not talk about that" — awkward silence
options.2: I shut down and the chat dies
options.3: I change subject abruptly with no bridge
options.4: I acknowledge and pivot — "Heavy — what brought you here today?"
options.5: I steer with a bridge question — smooth and kind

humor-without-overshare.prompt: I use humor without turning my life into their entertainment.

options.1: My funniest stories are also my most identifying
options.2: I roast myself with details strangers shouldn't store
options.3: I tell "you had to be there" stories that still reveal too much
options.4: I keep jokes generic — no names, no addresses
options.5: I'm funny on themes, not on my private file

end-conversation-kind.prompt: I can end a chat kindly without opening a new personal chapter.

byPlace.flight: Before landing, I wrap seatmate talk without trading contacts I don't want.
byPlace.queue: When my turn comes, I exit the line chat without oversharing to say goodbye.
byPlace.networking: I leave a mixer conversation with a clear close — not a late-night confessional.
byPlace.socialOnline: I end a DM thread without dumping one last secret "since we're chatting."

options.1: Goodbyes become overshares — "anyway my ex…"
options.2: I give my number or socials to escape, then dread pings
options.3: I linger and add one unnecessary personal detail
options.4: I close warm with a simple line and go
options.5: I end clean: gratitude, no new data

networking-vs-therapy.prompt: At professional events, I network — I don't treat strangers like my therapist.

byCounterpart.pleasant: Even with a kind stranger at an event, I don't turn career chat into trauma dump.
byCounterpart.prying: When someone at a mixer digs for dirt, I don't reward it with workplace secrets.
byCounterpart.professional: With a client or colleague type, I keep talk appropriate — wins and themes, not confessions.

options.1: I unload career fear, marriage stress, or health on a new contact
options.2: I share internal company dirt to bond
options.3: I slide into personal venting when alcohol or vibe shifts
options.4: I stay professional-friendly — industry talk, light personal
options.5: I keep the lane clear: connect, don't confess

online-dm-pace.prompt: With new online contacts, I pace intimacy — not instant best friends.

byPlace.flight: If a seatmate and I swap socials, I don't treat the first DM thread like a diary.
byPlace.queue: If we traded handles while waiting, I pace messages — no life story before we've earned it.
byPlace.networking: After an event follow-up online, I keep depth professional until trust is real.
byPlace.socialOnline: In new DMs, I don't match their life story in the first hour — I pace replies and depth.

options.1: I send long personal essays to people I just matched with
options.2: I share location, schedule, or photos before we've met or verified
options.3: I mirror their speed even when my gut says slow down
options.4: I reply shorter and slower until trust builds
options.5: I treat DMs like a front door — knock, don't move in

body-says-no.prompt: When my body says "don't share that," I listen before my mouth opens.

options.1: I ignore tight chest / nausea and talk anyway to be nice
options.2: I notice the feeling after I've already said it
options.3: I sometimes pause; sometimes people-please wins
options.4: I pause and shorten what I was about to say
options.5: I treat body signals as a hard stop — redirect or exit

too-many-questions.prompt: When question speed picks up, I slow the data flow.

byCounterpart.pleasant: When a friendly person asks rapid-fire personal stuff, I don't answer every one.
byCounterpart.prying: When someone interviews me, I name it and go vague — or leave.
byCounterpart.professional: When a work contact crosses into personal interrogation, I boundary without burning bridges.

options.1: I answer a rapid personal Q&A like a game show
options.2: I feel rude saying no, so I feed the curiosity
options.3: I answer some, dodge some — inconsistent filter
options.4: I answer one, then bridge to them or a neutral topic
options.5: I slow down: "Let's back up — we're just meeting"

flattery-for-info.prompt: When flattery comes with questions, I don't trade secrets for compliments.

options.1: Compliments loosen me — I share things I'd never share otherwise
options.2: I feel special and over-disclose to keep the praise coming
options.3: I notice sometimes after the fact
options.4: I thank them and keep answers generic
options.5: I treat charm + questions as a pattern — minimal data

alcohol-loosens.prompt: When drinks are involved, I keep the same filters — not louder privacy.

options.1: Happy hour turns into tell-all — coworkers, exes, money
options.2: One drink in and I'm showing photos or venting
options.3: I'm looser but try to catch myself mid-story
options.4: I drink socially and keep stories thematic
options.5: Alcohol doesn't get admin access to my life

recording-or-audience.prompt: When others might overhear or record, I shrink the detail.

byPlace.flight: On a plane, I assume rows nearby hear — I keep voice and detail down.
byPlace.queue: In public lines, I don't discuss sensitive topics at full volume.
byPlace.networking: At events with mics or cameras, I don't say what I'd regret on a clip.
byPlace.socialOnline: In group chats or lives, I don't share what I'd want private in DM.

options.1: I share sensitive stuff loudly or on hot mics
options.2: I forget phones pointed at me or stories being retold
options.3: I quiet down only after someone glances over
options.4: I check audience size and lower detail proactively
options.5: I assume ears and cameras — default to low detail

follow-up-contact.prompt: When someone asks to stay in touch, I choose channels I can actually boundary.

byCounterpart.pleasant: When a nice stranger wants my number, I offer a level I'm OK ignoring.
byCounterpart.prying: When a prying person pushes for Instagram or WhatsApp, I decline or use a public handle only.
byCounterpart.professional: When a work contact follows up, I use professional channels — not personal bleed.

options.1: I give primary phone/socials to almost everyone
options.2: I say yes to follow-ups I already dread
options.3: I give contact info then mute — messy
options.4: I offer LinkedIn or email instead of personal when unsure
options.5: I decide before sharing: do I want this person in my pocket?

share-to-fill-silence.prompt: When silence hits, I don't pay with private stories.

options.1: Silence panics me — I confess or overshare to fill it
options.2: I tell heavy stories because quiet feels rude
options.3: Sometimes I weather silence; sometimes I spill
options.4: I ask them something or comment on the setting
options.5: Silence is fine — I don't buy comfort with data

regret-after-chat.prompt: After stranger chats, I rarely think "why did I say that?"

options.1: I often replay conversations with cringe — too much shared
options.2: Regret hits weekly after small talk
options.3: Mixed — some chats fine, some haunt me
options.4: Occasional tweak, not a pattern
options.5: I leave chats feeling OK — bounded and kind

third-party-gossip.prompt: When gossip about someone else comes up, I don't add fuel or private facts.

options.1: I share dirt I shouldn't — names and stories that aren't mine
options.2: I "just vent" about coworkers or friends to strangers
options.3: I listen and add one detail I shouldn't
options.4: I stay neutral or change subject
options.5: I don't trade other people's privacy for bonding

professional-secrets.prompt: I don't leak work secrets to strangers — even casual ones.

byCounterpart.pleasant: Even with a friendly seatmate, I don't share unreleased products or internal numbers.
byCounterpart.prying: When someone fishes for company secrets, I don't bite — pleasant or not.
byCounterpart.professional: With industry peers, I keep NDAs and client trust — small talk isn't clearance.

options.1: I've shared confidential timelines, clients, or internal drama
options.2: I hint at things under NDA to sound important
options.3: I share when it feels "off the record" — it isn't
options.4: I speak in public knowledge only
options.5: Work secrets stay at work — strangers get zero leverage

emotional-dump.prompt: When I'm stressed, I don't unload on someone who can't hold it.

options.1: I cry or trauma-dump on seatmates, drivers, or new DMs
options.2: I treat any listener like free therapy
options.3: I vent edges of big feelings — then feel exposed
options.4: I acknowledge stress briefly and redirect
options.5: Heavy feelings go to chosen people — not random strangers

ask-before-advise.prompt: When strangers share problems, I don't bulldoze with advice — or mirror with my drama.

options.1: I one-up with my bigger story or fix them unprompted
options.2: I give long advice to someone who wanted small talk
options.3: I listen, then slip into my own overshare
options.4: I reflect once and ask if they want ideas
options.5: I match energy: empathy, not takeover or confession swap

public-place-volume.prompt: In public, I keep sensitive topics at a volume strangers shouldn't inherit.

byPlace.flight: On a flight, I don't discuss medical, legal, or relationship crises at seat volume.
byPlace.queue: In a crowded line, I don't narrate private calls or fights aloud.
byPlace.networking: At a hotel bar event, I remember tables overlap — detail stays low.
byPlace.socialOnline: In public comments or stories, I don't post what belongs in a private chat.

options.1: Strangers could quote my phone call or argument
options.2: I discuss money, health, or sex where everyone hears
options.3: I quiet down only when directly embarrassed
options.4: I step aside or lower voice for sensitive bits
options.5: Public = low detail — save depth for private space

leave-with-dignity.prompt: When a chat turns uncomfortable, I leave without over-explaining my life.

options.1: I stay and overshare to justify leaving — makes it worse
options.2: I ghost mid-chat without a word
options.3: I make excuses that add new personal facts
options.4: I use a simple out — polite, firm, minimal info
options.5: I exit clean: boundary without autobiography
